subject: HIPAA scope, BAA request & DPIA coordination for patient-chat integration
messages:
From: Alice Wu <alice.wu@cerebrahealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HIPAA scope / BAA request and DPIA trigger for patient-chat feature

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the Cerebra product team is excited about the patient-chat assistant. Before we proceed to a pilot, our Security and Privacy teams need clarity on a few items so we can evaluate BAA eligibility and whether a DPIA is required on our side. High-level asks: 

- Does Redwood ever persist PHI beyond request/response lifetime for hosted API customers? If so, under what conditions and retention controls?
- We need a copy of your SOC 2 Type II report and any SIG/CAIQ responses you have completed recently.
- Our legal team requires a BAA template and confirmation of whether Redwood will sign the standard Cerebra BAA or if we should use Redwood's form.
- Attached is a high-level dataflow diagram for our integration (cerebra_dataflow_v1.pdf). Please confirm where PHI is in transit vs at rest, and recommend deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private) to meet a HIPAA covered-entity requirement.

We'd like to kick off a short DPIA workshop if this looks like it could process PHI. Can your team propose next steps and an estimate for evidence turnaround?

Appreciate it —
Alice
Security Program Manager
Cerebra Health

--
Attachment: cerebra_dataflow_v1.pdf (diagram, 245 KB)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Wu <alice.wu@cerebrahealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HIPAA scope / BAA request and DPIA trigger for patient-chat feature

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear note and the dataflow diagram. We're happy to help. Quick answers up front: 

- Hosted API: by default we do not retain customer input/output for production hosted customers beyond short-term processing (ephemeral KV), unless a customer opts into logging/analytics. For workloads requiring PHI handling we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) to ensure data isolation.
- We can provide our most recent SOC 2 Type II report and a completed SIG questionnaire. CAIQ is available on request; we'll include it in the evidence packet.
- We have a standard Redwood BAA that we use for most customers; we can either sign Cerebra's BAA or provide our template and work through redlines. Legal prefers starting from our template for speed but we'll accommodate your preference.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Dev (cc'd) will confirm recommended deployment and whether any product configuration is required to ensure no retained PHI.
2) I'll share SOC2 & CAIQ artifacts and a copy of Redwood's BAA template via DocuSign for signature.
3) If a DPIA is needed, Marissa can run a 60-minute workshop with your Privacy lead to capture processing details and mitigation recommendations.

Can you confirm whether Cerebra intends to store transcripts on your side (and for how long) or if the transcripts will be read-only ephemeral messages? That will affect the DPIA scope.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

--
(Attachment plan: redwood_baa_template.pdf to be shared after internal review)

- Cerebra will store chat transcripts for care continuity. Initial retention policy will be 6 months; that may change with legal input.
- We prefer starting from Redwood's BAA if that will speed signature.
- Attached: a short DPIA summary we drafted (cerebra_dpia_summary.docx) to help scope the workshop.

Also please flag whether dedicated/private deployment is required for HIPAA compliance or whether hosted with specific config is sufficient.

Appreciate a timeline for when we can expect the evidence and a target date to sign the BAA (we'd like it in place before pilot start: target 2027-04-29).

Thanks,
Alice

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HIPAA scope / BAA request and DPIA trigger for patient-chat feature

Hi Alice — thanks for the DPIA summary and the retention note. A few concrete points and what we'll deliver by end of day Friday: 

- Retention: Because Cerebra will persist transcripts for 6 months, we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private for production PHI to remove multi-tenant retention risks. Hosted API can be configured to avoid retention, but we (and auditors) typically recommend Dedicated/Private for covered-entity workloads.
- Subprocessors: Our current list of subprocessors is in the SOC2 packet; the only one that commonly affects text processing is a managed log-aggregation service (we can redact PII before logs are sent). We'll highlight subprocessor details in the evidence bundle.
- Evidence deliverables (target: 2027-04-23 EOD): SOC 2 Type II redacted report, completed SIG questionnaire, CAIQ export, redwood_security_whitepaper.pdf, and a copy of Redwood's BAA template (we'll attach a pre-signed PDF for speed: redwood_signed_baa_template.pdf).
- Operational controls: we'll include recommended configuration: request-level encryption in transit (TLS), customer-managed KMS for Private deployments, KV caching disabled for hosted, and an inbound/outbound filtering rule set for PHI PII detection.

I'll open a secure evidence folder and a Jira ticket for follow-ups: SEC-939. Evelyn will handle the BAA signature via DocuSign (link below). If you want, Marissa can schedule the DPIA workshop for next week.

Links: DocuSign envelope: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/1234-CRB-BAA
Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-939

Regards,
Dev Patel
